note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Adult patient with one-week history of sore throat followed by dry cough and intermittent exertional shortness of breath; assessed as likely self-limiting upper respiratory infection, given symptomatic advice, acetaminophen recommended, and a sick note provided; advised to seek in-person review if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Sore throat for about 1 week, then dry cough beginning 1–2 days after sore throat.
  - Intermittent shortness of breath and wheeze started ~3–4 days ago (after onset of cough).
  - Mild chest pain described “a bit of both” with wheeze.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Sore throat began last week (patient approximated “last week, Friday or Thursday”).
  - Dry cough started Saturday or Sunday (1–2 days after sore throat).
  - Shortness of breath began ~3–4 days ago, shortly after cough onset.
  - Feverish for the first ~3 days, then fever resolved.
  - Symptoms have been variable: some days better, some days worse; patient stayed off work 2–4 days total (stated 2 days this week, earlier said 3–4 days off work).
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - No specific exacerbating or relieving factors documented.
  - Symptoms are similar throughout the day (not worse at night).
- Associated symptoms:
  - Intermittent headache (present earlier, not currently).
  - Reduced appetite recently; no reported weight loss.
- Systems review / pertinent negatives:
  - No sputum production; no hemoptysis.
  - No sinus congestion or nasal symptoms.
  - No rashes.
  - No palpable neck lumps per patient.
  - No unexplained weight loss reported.
  - No history of asthma.
  - No recent travel outside Europe; born in US, moved to UK ~12 years ago.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.
- No history of asthma.
- Current medications: none reported.
- Allergies: peanuts.

Social History:
- Born in the United States; moved to the UK ~12 years ago.
- Recent travel: travel to Europe only (no exotic travel).
- Tobacco/substance use:
  - Not a regular smoker; reports smoking “once or twice in Amsterdam” historically.
  - No known asbestos exposure.
- Employment: works (requested sick note); specific occupation not documented.

Family History:
- Mother had lung cancer.
- No other family history of clotting disorders or other significant illnesses mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals documented.
- No physical examination findings documented (throat and chest not examined during consult; patient reported no neck lumps).

Investigations:
- No investigations, imaging, or laboratory results documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute sore throat with dry cough — likely viral upper respiratory infection (clinician impression).
  - Plan:
    - Reassurance provided; clinician expects improvement within 4–5 days.
    - Symptomatic treatment recommended: paracetamol (acetaminophen) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Advise rest and increased fluid intake.
    - Sick note provided to allow time off work — duration not documented.
    - Return/seek assessment if not improving in expected timeframe.
- Issue 2: Shortness of breath with wheeze and mild chest pain (new, exertional rather than at rest).
  - Assessment:
    - Described as present but not severe; patient remains able to perform activities such as walking and exercise with some unusual breathlessness.
  - Plan:
    - Advise in-person review (GP or urgent assessment) if breathlessness worsens, acutely increases, or if sudden change occurs.
    - If symptoms persist or do not improve, arrange physical examination and further assessment.
- Issue 3: Patient concern regarding tuberculosis and lung cancer (family history of lung cancer).
  - Assessment:
    - Clinician not currently concerned about tuberculosis or lung cancer given clinical course, provided reassurance conditional on improvement.
  - Plan:
    - Reassurance given; advise follow-up and in-person review if symptoms fail to resolve or worsen to reassess and consider investigations.
- General plan items:
  - Provide symptomatic care, safety-netting advice, and arrange/advise in-person assessment if deterioration or lack of improvement.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, respiratory rate, heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation) not documented.
  - Physical examination findings (throat inspection, lung auscultation) not documented.
  - Exact duration of sick note not documented.
  - Medication dosing, route, and frequency for paracetamol/acetaminophen not documented.
  - No diagnostic tests ordered or results available (e.g., chest x-ray, COVID/viral testing, or inflammatory markers).
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Patient initially responded “No” to shortness of breath, then immediately stated “Yes” and described SOB — conflict noted.
  - Number of days off work: patient variously stated “three or four of those days” and later “I stayed home from work two days this week” — discrepancy noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio/transcript is overall intelligible with minor hesitations and repeated phrases; clinical details are extractable.
